cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 is the main law protecting consumers. It applies to goods, services, and digital content purchased in the UK.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Three key rights for goods: they must be as described (match their description), fit for purpose (do what the buyer reasonably expects), and of satisfactory quality (meet the standard a reasonable person would accept).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: If goods are faulty: within 30 days — full refund; after 30 days but within 6 months — repair or replacement (retailer chooses); if repair/replacement fails — refund (with deduction for use after 6 months).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill, at a reasonable price, and within a reasonable time. If not, the consumer is entitled to a repeat performance or price reduction.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Online shoppers have additional rights: 14-day cancellation period for most goods and services (distance selling regulations), and the trader pays return postage for faulty goods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) enforces consumer protection law and can take businesses to court for unfair practices.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Trading Standards (local authority) investigates complaints about unfair trading, unsafe products, and rogue traders. They can prosecute and issue fines.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Citizens Advice provides free information and support on consumer issues, helping people understand their rights and how to make complaints.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) regulates financial products and services, protecting consumers from mis-selling and financial fraud.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Consumer responsibilities: read contracts carefully, pay for goods and services, report unsafe products, make informed choices, and treat businesses fairly.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Ethical consumerism considers the social and environmental impact of purchases — fair trade, sustainable sourcing, and avoiding companies with poor labour practices.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Many consumers do not know their rights — surveys show low awareness of the Consumer Rights Act, particularly among young people and vulnerable groups.

cards.front: What should you know about citizenship studies exam tips — consumer rights?
cards.back: 1. For Consumer Rights questions, use citizenship terminology and reference democratic processes accurately 2. Consider multiple viewpoints — including those you disagree with 3. Link Consumer Rights to current affairs and real-world examples where possible 4. When evaluating, consider both rights and responsibilities 5. Structure longer answers: identify the issue, analyse different perspectives, reach a justified view
Evaluate the effectiveness of consumer protection in the UK. [12 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding — 30%): You need to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of consumer rights, including key concepts, legal frameworks, and institutional structures.
